title: How Visko streams real-time world models on Google Cloud TPUs
summary:
Editor's note: Generative AI startups are moving rapidly beyond static clip generation to build interactive, real-time worlds. In this technical deep dive, we explore how AI startup Visko collaborated with Google Cloud TPU engineers to deploy Orbis — its continuously streaming Live World Model—on Cloud TPUs, going from initial kickoff to production handover in just 30 days.

What makes a live video world model so challenging to serve in production? The bottleneck isn't average throughput — it's beating a relentless real-time clock. Unlike offline video generators where a user submits a prompt and waits in a queue, a live world model streams continuously. Every new chunk of video and synchronized audio must finish rendering before the viewer finishes watching the previous one, or the world freezes.

Today, we're excited to share how Visko, an AI startup pioneering interactive world models, teamed up with Google Cloud to solve this exact challenge. Working side by side, Visko and Google Cloud engineers deployed Visko's end-to-end live inference pipeline — combining video generation, super-resolution upscaling, and synchronized audio—onto a single Cloud TPU slice. Together, the teams brought end-to-end generation down, rendering at 1.07x playback speed.

Here is an inside look at how we engineered the pipeline to hit that milestone in a single month, the architectural optimizations that moved the needle, and practical lessons for other startups building ultra-low-latency generative AI on Google Cloud.

Redefining interactive media with Live World Models

While most generative video platforms focus on rendering fixed, pre-baked clips, Visko is building what it calls Live Models: video world models that generate continuously and respond on the fly.

Visko's flagship model, Orbis, streams live video starting from a single text or image prompt. As the stream plays, viewers can enter new steering prompts in real time, dynamically evolving the scene without restarting or breaking continuity. For instance, in one test session, the livestream opens on a cat napping beside a crackling fireplace; when the viewer steers the scene to introduce a bowl of food, the bowl materializes seamlessly, and the cat stretches, stands up, and meows.

Since launching its public demo on September 1, 2026, Orbis has unlocked new possibilities across interactive entertainment, live commerce, AI companions, immersive education, and robotics simulation. To scale these interactive sessions reliably, Visko partnered with Google Cloud TPU engineers in August 2026 to port the Orbis live pipeline to Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU). Within 30 days, the full multimodal pipeline was running in real time on TPUs.

Visko’s ambition is to power a new generation of interactive worlds that people can step into and shape in real time. Streaming continuous video and audio under a strict clock is a fundamentally different system challenge than offline clip generation. Working side by side with Google Cloud's TPU engineers, we brought the full Orbis pipeline to TPUs in just 30 days — giving us the low-latency compute and memory bandwidth required to bring Live Models to creators and developers at scale.

"Visko is bringing an exciting new class of real-time, steerable workloads to the Cloud TPU ecosystem. By co-engineering their live multimodal pipeline on a singleTPU slice using JAX, torchax, and custom Pallas kernels, we proved how quickly a lean startup team can go from PyTorch prototype to render at 1.07x playback speed on Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer."
– Dave Elliott, Head of Developer Advocacy for AI, Google Cloud 

Live video is a hard-deadline problem

When you serve an offline clip generator, latency is forgiving — the user waits once while the backend processes frames. A live world model has no waiting room.

Every single chunk must be denoised, decoded from latents, upscaled to 1664x936 (at 18 fps), and paired with generated audio faster than realtime playback speed, for as long as the session runs.

Two structural constraints make live world models far more demanding than standard batch inference:

  • Batch size of one: Each live stream represents an individual viewer's interactive session. You cannot mask latency by grouping dozens of concurrent requests into a massive batch — the standard playbook for keeping AI accelerators saturated.

  • Strict sequential dependency: Every chunk depends directly on the one before it. Because the video model maintains a rolling memory of recent video latents so that chunk N+1 smoothly continues the action from chunk N, you cannot pre-render chunks out of order or parallelize across future timestamps.

For startup infrastructure engineers coming from LLM serving, it helps to think of live world modeling not as a tokens-per-second throughput benchmark, but as an unforgiving per-step latency SLO.

Architecting the multimodal pipeline on a single TPU slice

To keep infrastructure lean and cost-effective as Visko scales, the team designed the live pipeline to chain three distinct generative models on a single Cloud TPU slice running in BF16 precision.

When a viewer submits an initial prompt or a live steering update, all three generative models — the core video diffusion model, the super-resolution upscaler, and the audio generator — share the same chips, taking turns on the hardware for each chunk.

To combine rapid startup iteration with bare-metal accelerator speed, the software stack is built on three open-source pillars:

  • JAX: Google's high-performance Python array library for accelerators, compiled into optimized machine code by the XLA compiler.

  • torchax: An interoperability layer that runs PyTorch models directly on Cloud TPUs via JAX, enabling startup teams to bring existing PyTorch components over without an upfront, ground-up rewrite.

  • Pallas: The custom kernel programming language for TPUs in JAX.

Real-time performance breakdown: Hitting the clock 

By profiling and optimizing each stage on a single slice in BF16, the engineering team achieved a total per-chunk latency of under the target while — maintaining roughly 7% headroom to absorb variance during live streaming:

Because video denoising accounts for nearly two-thirds of the total compute budget, that stage became the primary focus of our kernel and parallelism optimizations.

Inside the stack: Three optimizations that unlocked real-time streaming

1. Ulysses context parallelism across all TPU chips

A video chunk expands into a massive sequence of spatiotemporal tokens inside the video transformer. To distribute that workload across the TPU chips at batch size 1, the team implemented Ulysses context parallelism.

Instead of splitting model weights, Ulysses splits the token sequence across chips. Immediately before the attention layer, a high-speed all-to-all interconnect exchange regroups the tensors so that each chip holds the entire video sequence, but only for one-quarter of the attention heads. After each chip computes attention over the full sequence for its assigned heads, a second all-to-all exchange restores the sequence-split layout for the feed-forward layers.

2. Custom Pallas splash attention from MaxDiffusion

To accelerate the attention computation itself, the team integrated a custom Pallas splash attention kernel from MaxDiffusion, Google Cloud's open-source reference library for diffusion models on Cloud TPU.

Splash attention brings FlashAttention-style tiling to TPU architecture: rather than materializing the full quadratic attention matrix in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), it computes attention in compact tiles that remain inside ultra-fast on-chip VMEM. Startup teams can drop the exact kernel used in this port straight into their own pipelines via custom_splash_attention.py.

3. A 5.8x audio speedup by moving from torchax to pure JAX

We first brought all three Orbis models onto Cloud TPU with torchax, which runs PyTorch code on TPU through JAX and XLA without a rewrite. For the video and upscaling models, torchax paired with Pallas attention kernels met our latency target directly, and both stay in torchax in the final pipeline.

Only the audio model needed a rewrite. Moving the audio stage from torchax to native JAX made it 5.8x faster and brought the full pipeline under the playback deadline.

Field notes for AI builders: Cloud TPU lessons

Takeaways from tuning live multimodal inference on Cloud TPU:

  • Ulysses context parallelism for single stream video: At batch size 1, splitting the token sequence across chips with all-to-all interconnect exchanges was faster than both tensor parallelism and ring attention.
  • Native BF16 for continuous streams: FP8 quantization cuts memory bandwidth pressure, but small quantization errors build up across chunks in a continuous stream. Native BF16 kept visual quality intact within the latency budget.
  • Selective JAX ports: torchax kept the video and upscaling models in PyTorch, so the team only rewrote the audio bottleneck in native JAX.
  • XLA compilation caching: The first boot spends a few minutes compiling XLA graphs. Caching compiled artifacts brings worker restarts under a minute.

Building real-time generative models on Cloud TPU? Start here

If your startup is pushing the boundaries of live video, world models, or ultra-low-latency multimodal inference, you can build with the same toolkit that powered Visko's port:

  • Accelerate diffusion attention out of the box: Grab the open-source splash attention kernel used in this collaboration from MaxDiffusion, and explore the Pallas documentation to write custom TPU kernels.

  • Migrate PyTorch fast, then optimize selectively: Bring your existing PyTorch models onto TPU quickly with torchax, pinpoint bottlenecks with the Cloud TPU Profiler, and port latency-critical stages to native JAX.

  • Spin up TPUs on demand: Use TPU Flex-start VMs to provision TPU capacity for short development and benchmarking runs without a long-term reservation.

  • Scale with Google for Startups: Early-stage AI startups looking for cloud credits, technical mentorship, and access to Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer stack can apply to the Google for Startups Cloud Program.

Special thanks to the Visko.ai team for the close technical partnership, and to the Google Cloud TPU engineers who lead the project including: Yixin Shi, James Huang, and Elisa Tsai.

title: What the Gemini agent means for startups
summary:
Small teams, short runway, and constant pressure to ship faster — it’s the reality we see every day among the founders we work with at Google for Startups. When you are building a company from the ground up, every hour spent on operational overhead or infrastructure plumbing is an hour taken away from your core product.

Last week at Gemini at Work 2026, we introduced the Gemini agent: a single, universal agent designed to work both as your personal assistant and as a dedicated member of your team. And this week, we made our new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, widely available — trained to maintain context across long, multi-step tasks.

Here is a look at how the Gemini agent works, five practical takeaways for founders, and how startups are already using it to punch above their weight.

What is the Gemini agent?

Instead of prompting separate chatbots for writing, coding, and data analysis, the Gemini agent is a single agent that takes high-level objectives and returns finished work. Three principles define it:

  • Unified: A single agent can now handle knowledge work, data analysis, creative asset generation, and writing and running code. For complex jobs, it dynamically spins up temporary, job-specific sub-agents and coordinates their work in parallel or in sequence.

  • Omnipresent access: It works across the surfaces you use every day — on the web, command line, desktop, and mobile, as well as natively inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Chat, and Calendar.

  • Persistent: It runs in the cloud with continuous memory across four dimensions (session, semantic, procedural, and episodic). It onboards itself like a new hire — learning your team, tools, and business context so you don't have to re-explain your startup with every prompt, and keeping multi-day tasks moving even after you close your laptop.

For founders wearing five hats at once, Gemini works like a digital chief of staff that's already briefed on your calendar, projects and documents. Ask it to research market trends, build a financial model in Sheets and turn both into a pitch deck, without repeating what the project or goals are at each step. It also works ahead of you. When an investor emails asking for your latest product update as a deck, Gemini spots the request and offers to handle it; one click and it comes back with completed work, ready for sharing or review.

Five takeaways for startups

1. Coworker agents and skills help you scale your output

Beyond personal assistance, you can create persistent coworker agents that work with your entire team. Each agent comes with its own Workspace account, email address, Drive storage, and directory presence. You can define a specific role — such as a launch coordinator, QA triager, or financial analyst — and your teammates can add agents to a Chat space or @mention it in a Google Doc comment to delegate work.

You can also equip agents with reusable skills — or let Gemini write skills for itself as it learns your processes. For example, with operational reporting skills connected to BigQuery and the Knowledge Catalog, anyone on your team can ask a plain-language question to build and save a live report. Once saved, those reports run on demand without incurring additional token costs. Gemini also offers pre-built specializations, starting with legal and financial services.

  • What it means for startups: Coworker agents can immediately increase the capacity of your teams, and skills can standardize repeatable processes like investor and operational reporting without burning tokens on every run.

2. Open and third-party model choice

Gemini is the agent, and the model underneath is your choice. As startup architectures mature, sending every task to a single frontier model quickly eats into gross margins. With the Gemini agent, you can dynamically route workloads across Gemini models, third-party models like Anthropic’s Claude, and lightweight open models like Gemma.

  • What it means for startups: You get flexibility without lock-in. You can optimize your cost per task — using compact models for high-volume, deterministic jobs and frontier models for complex reasoning — and swap models as your product evolves without rebuilding your workflows.

3. Connected to your services and tools 

An agent is only as useful as the systems it can reach. In addition to Google Workspace, the Gemini agent connects directly to your engineering, data, and business stack, including partner solutions:

  • Development and collaboration: Git, Slack, Jira and more 

  • Data and local files: BigQuery, Postgres, Snowflake, Databricks, and more alongside files on your desktop

  • Custom tools via MCP: Any Model Context Protocol (MCP) server inside or outside your network so your engineers can build and share internal tools.

What it means for startups: Instead of spending engineering cycles maintaining custom connectors, your team can plug the agent straight into your existing codebase, databases, and MCP tools so it can act on live data wherever it lives.

4. Built-in security and governance

For B2B startups, the enterprise security audit is often where deals stall. Under the hood, every agent is assigned a cryptographic Agent Identity for clear audit trails, runs inside an isolated sandbox, and protected with built-in prompt injection defenses. External traffic is routed through Agent Gateway, allowing you to enforce governance policies. And managing coworker agents is as straightforward as managing users today, since they all have a Workspace account.

  • What it means for startups: When an enterprise buyer’s CISO asks how your AI workflows handle data privacy, prompt injection, and access control, you have an enterprise-grade architecture ready — helping you clear procurement hurdles.

5. Protect your runway with real-time cost controls

Autonomous agents that run sub-agents for hours or days can quickly run up a bill if a loop goes unchecked. You can now set hard, real-time spend caps directly in the Cloud Billing Console; if a cap is reached, the project's agent automatically pauses so a bug never turns into a billing surprise. Underneath, Gemini runs on Google’s specialized AI infrastructure, including our inference-optimized TPU 8i, which delivers 80% better performance-per-dollar than the prior generation.

  • What it means for startups: You and your developers can experiment with long-running, parallel agentic loops with a built-in financial safety net that protects your cash reserves and builds confidence with your backers.

Founders already building

Startups and AI-native innovators are already putting Gemini to work. Immersive storytelling platform Whenere used Dreamlands, an agentic 3D worldbuilding platform built on Gemini platform, to bring Pride and Prejudice to Fortnite — with Gemini generating textures for each new object in about 7 seconds for under 10 cents; one artist created nearly 250 custom assets in a single day and completed a historically accurate estate in under a week. They join application-building platform Lovable and fellow startups and innovators including  OpenEvidence, Recursion, and Replit and more.

Build with Google for Startups

The agentic era gives lean teams the leverage to punch far above their weight — whether you’re deploying coworker agents to cover internal operations or building agentic workflows directly into your product.

While these new Gemini agent capabilities are not publicly available yet, startups can contact our sales team to learn more and discuss how to get ready. In the meantime, you can explore the Google for Startups program to access credits, hands-on technical guidance, mentorship, global founder community programs and more.

title: Predictable AI spend in BigQuery: Introducing cost management for generative AI functions
summary:
The generative AI functions in BigQuery (AI.GENERATE, AI.IF, AI.CLASSIFY, AI.SCORE, and more) bring large language models (LLMs) directly into your SQL, so a single query can classify millions of support tickets or score each product review for sentiment. However, because these functions are billed by the token, scaling them across massive datasets highlights the importance of managing your budget proactively. 

We recently announced the general availability (GA) of token-based cost management for BigQuery generative AI functions: daily quotas that let administrators set self-serve guardrails on AI token consumption, so teams can innovate while staying within your budget. In this blog, we provide an overview of cost management for BigQuery generative AI functions, walk through a few practical examples, and share resources to help you get started. Let’s jump in.  

Quotas for managing costs

Four daily quotas, managed through the Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) quota system, provide controls at the project level and the per-user level. Per-user limits apply to each user within a project, not across your organization.

Quota name

Metric

Scope

Default value

AI input tokens per day

Input tokens used by the LLM

Per day, per project

200 billion

AI input tokens per day per user

Input tokens used by the LLM

Per day, per project, per user

150 billion

AI output tokens per day

Output and thinking tokens used by the LLM

Per day, per project, per project

20 billion

AI output tokens per day per user

Output and thinking tokens used by the LLM

Per day, per project, per user

15 billion

Key details:

  • The quotas are global. Usage is summed across all regions, so costs can't pile up unnoticed in a region you weren't watching.

  • Output quotas include "thinking" tokens. Reasoning tokens count toward your output quota, just as they count toward your Gemini platform bill.

Which functions are covered?

The quotas apply to these BigQuery functions that perform LLM-backed generation:

  • AI.GENERATE

  • AI.GENERATE_TABLE

  • AI.GENERATE_TEXT (and its alias ML.GENERATE_TEXT)

  • AI.CLASSIFY

  • AI.IF

  • AI.SCORE

  • AI.AGG

What's not covered: Embedding functions such as AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING (also available as ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) and AI.EMBED are not subject to these quotas, because they run on different, substantially cheaper models.

Managing your quotas

Administrators can view and adjust the quotas directly in the Google Cloud console as workloads change, with no support case required.

  1. Navigate to IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits.

  2. Filter by service and select BigQuery API.

  3. Sort by the Name column to bring the four AI quotas to the top.

4. Find the quota, for example AI input tokens per day.

5. Open the three-dot menu and choose Edit quota.

From there:

  • To tighten cost control, lower a quota. This takes effect immediately with no approval needed.

  • To support higher usage, request an increase from the same page. Many requests are auto-approved; larger increases may go through a quick review.

You'll need the right permissions. You need one of: Owner, Editor, Quota Administrator (roles/servicemanagement.quotaAdmin), or Service Usage Admin (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin).

Prefer automation? You can also manage these quotas programmatically through the Cloud Quotas API, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform to apply consistent guardrails across projects.

Monitoring usage

Beyond setting limits, the Quotas & System Limits page displays your historical token consumption so you can quickly detect spikes and right-size your budgets. Use these trends to see how new generative AI workloads and data pipelines affect your overall token usage.

For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the BigQuery documentation on controlling costs with token quotas.

Token quotas vs. billing spend caps

Token quotas aren't the only cost guardrail in Google Cloud.

  • Token quotas (this feature) are preventive and AI-specific. BigQuery tracks token usage during query execution and stops work close to the limit, with separate limits per project and per user.

  • Cloud Billing spend caps operate on dollars at the project and service level and can automatically block usage when a threshold is reached. They're a broad, financial backstop rather than a precise usage control, and because enforcement is not instant, some overages are incurred.

Use token quotas as your first line of defense for AI spend, and a spend cap as a project-wide safety net.

How enforcement works

Quotas are enforced by stopping work rather than letting a query run past your limit. A query is rejected up front with a QuotaExceeded error only if a quota it needs is already exhausted. Otherwise, it starts, and if a quota runs out mid-query, BigQuery stops sending new LLM calls:

  • Functions that support max_error_ratio (such as AI.IF) return partial results if unprocessed rows stay within the ratio, and otherwise fail.

  • General-purpose functions (such as AI.GENERATE) still succeed. Skipped rows have no generated value, and their status field contains the quota-exceeded error.

For details, see quota enforcement behavior in the documentation.

Sizing your input data: AI.COUNT_TOKENS

To choose quota values, it helps to know how much text your workloads send to a model. The AI.COUNT_TOKENS function helps with this.

AI.COUNT_TOKENS returns the number of tokens a model's tokenizer produces for a text string, without making a billable generation call. Run it over a column to measure your input data:

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "-- Count the input text tokens for each product review\r\nSELECT\r\n SUM(\r\n AI.COUNT_TOKENS(\r\n CONCAT('Classify the sentiment of this review as positive, negative, or neutral: ', review_text),\r\n\r\n endpoint => 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite').result) AS total_input_tokens\r\nFROM\r\n `my_project.my_dataset.product_reviews`;"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f309ddbe150>)])]>

The count is a lower bound on input tokens. It doesn't include output or thinking tokens, the instructions each AI function adds around your input, or non-text inputs such as images. Use it to:

  • Gauge the input side of a workload before you launch it.

  • Right-size your quotas together with a small sample run that measures actual input and output usage.

  • Translate tokens into dollars using the published Gemini platform pricing for your model.

From tokens to budget: a worked example

Suppose you want to keep a project's daily AI spend around $100 with the Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite model. As of today's published pricing (BigQuery processes in batch which provides a 50% discount):

  • Input tokens: $0.125 per 1 million tokens

  • Output tokens (response + reasoning): $0.75 per 1 million tokens

If a small sample run shows an average 100:1 input-to-output token ratio, you can solve for a daily budget:

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'Cost: 0.125 × I + 0.75 × O = 100 (I, O in millions of tokens)\r\nRatio: I = 100 × O'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f309e0c2610>)])]>

Solving gives about 754 million input tokens and 7.54 million output tokens per day. Set AI input tokens per day and AI output tokens per day to these values to hold the project near $100/day. If a project uses models with different prices, budget per model or blend the rates.

Best practices for managing AI cost

  • Start with per-user quotas. They stop one user or runaway experiment from draining the project's budget.

  • Measure before you scale. Use AI.COUNT_TOKENS to size your input, then check a small sample run in the usage chart before setting limits.

  • Mind the output side. Output tokens cost more. Where a function accepts max_output_tokens, set it to bound generation length.

  • Monitor and iterate. Adjust limits as real usage and budgets change.

Get started

Token-based cost management is available now. To begin:

  1. Open IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits in the Google Cloud Console and filter by BigQuery API.

  2. Review the four AI-related token quotas and set limits that match your budget.

  3. Use AI.COUNT_TOKENS to size your input data.

For the full details, see the documentation on controlling generative AI costs.

With token-based guardrails in place, your teams can use generative AI in BigQuery with the cost predictability your organization needs.

title: Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud, built to help solve your business’ hardest problems
summary:
Last week we announced that Gemini Enterprise has evolved to make it even simpler to get work done, and introduced the Gemini agent, your new universal agent for work. It's always on and ready to answer your questions. It will write code, complete longer and more complex tasks, or perform whatever you need to get the job done, all from a single prompt box. And model intelligence underpins it all.

To enable a new frontier of work, we are making our new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, available on Google Cloud. 

We trained Argon to work with both depth and precision, which allows it to maintain context across long, multi-step tasks which are reinforced with strong domain expertise along the way. Whether your team is running complex software builds, handling detailed financial and legal work, or deploying cybersecurity tools like CodeMender, Argon helps your teams maintain focus from start to finish. 

Four ways Argon changes how your business works

1. Hand off your hardest work

Your teams already use Gemini for business to answer questions and draft content. With Argon, they can hand off the deep, multi-step work that used to take hours or days, and get back finished work they can use.

Argon reads long documents that mix text, tables, charts and images, and turns them into one clear output grounded in those sources. It can pull findings from many sources into a single structured answer, analyze data over time, and write stronger legal, finance, and executive documents. On long tasks, it keeps going until the job is done. We trained Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause for confirmation before taking irreversible steps, and it tells you when it couldn't find something or finish a task.

Customers who tested Argon tell us it excels at turning huge, unstructured inputs into cohesive outputs. 

"As software development becomes more agentic, teams need models that can support long-running, multi-step work across all stages of the development lifecycle. Gemini 4 Argon is designed to help organizations bring AI into development, security, and operations while keeping it within established enterprise workflows and controls.” – Stuart Moncada, VP, GitLab.

2. Precise, verifiable results on the work that drives your business

In finance, legal, tax, and other regulated work, calculations and data extraction need to be precise, repeatable, and verifiable. 

For financial quantitative work, Argon can help automate multi-step ledger reconciliations, spreadsheet formulas, and variance analyses. It delivers high calculation integrity, citation fidelity, and formula accuracy across quantitative models. The proof is in the numbers: Argon leads on the Vals Index, which measures economic impact across finance, coding, legal, and tax work.

In legal research, Argon can help legal teams review case law and regulatory filings to pull out verified citations and key precedents. It leads on domain-specific evaluations like Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark for legal research and drafting, with strong citation fidelity and direct answers when helping teams evaluate complex legal precedents. 

"Gemini 4 Argon shows how much progress Google has made on agentic legal reasoning. We saw substantial improvements over Gemini 3.1 Pro across our legal agent evaluations, particularly in corporate M&A, data privacy and cybersecurity, and EC/VC. Accuracy also held up on long-document analysis, an encouraging result for lawyers working through detailed transactional matters." – Niko Grupen, Head of Applied Research, Harvey.

“We collaborated with Google on NowAI-Bench to help shape Gemini 4 for key enterprise work. In early access, it delivered roughly 20% improved task success than Gemini 3.8 Flash, with standout gains in HR and customer service. On the ServiceNow AI Platform, our L1 Service Desk AI specialist brings Google’s most advanced intelligence, governed and secure, turning tasks into fully autonomous work.” - Nenshad Bardoliwalla, Senior Vice President, AI Products, ServiceNow.

3. Build and ship products faster

Argon is built to handle complex, multi-step projects from start to finish. Our customers consistently ask for intelligence that can break down goals, track progress, and update multiple files at the same time.

"Gemini 4 Argon handles complex tasks reliably, from 3D games to rich animations. In Figma Make, it helps teams turn their most ambitious, multi-step ideas into impressive prototypes.” – Loredana Crisan, Chief Design Officer, Figma. 

To see how well Argon handles this, we put it to work on our own tools. The team behind our open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) set out to reduce framework overhead and improve code performance while maintaining full compatibility with existing applications. Working autonomously overnight within automated testing guardrails, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python, that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and speed up cold imports by 21%. To learn more, read the engineering deep dive here.

Across Google, engineering teams using Argon in Google Antigravity have increased agentic code submissions by more than 35% while cutting code rollbacks by nearly a third. The Chrome team used Argon to finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files in Chromium's 40 million-line codebase, completing months of work in weeks. Argon's improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision and visual coding also make it faster to go from idea to working prototype. 

For more advanced algorithms, our code optimization and discovery agent AlphaEvolve uses Argon to deliver strong performance improvements across real-world enterprise workloads, including factory scheduling, logistics, game code speed-ups, and chip layout — as well as complex mathematical benchmarks, and more. 

To learn how to best use Argon, check out the developer's guide.

4. Stronger defense for your code and business 

While Argon has cyber mitigations that block offensive tasks such as pentesting and exploitation, you can still take full advantage of Argon’s defensive capabilities using CodeMender to find and fix vulnerabilities, or use Argon with your own security harness. It ties for first place on CWE-Bench v1 with a top score of 68% for remediating security vulnerabilities.

"We are integrating Gemini 4 Argon into MarketingX for automated codebase security audits. In our evaluations, the model successfully identified 100% of top-priority vulnerabilities with 0% fabricated vulnerabilities across verified claims. This precision unlocks proactive, code-level security for our customers before deployment.” - Yunus Emre, Chief AI Officer of AI Lab, HubX.

Security also means being able to trust Argon inside your own environment. Argon is our most resilient model yet against indirect prompt injections, where malicious instructions or context are used to hijack a model’s behavior. It leads the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%. That matters when Argon reads email, documents and webpages that may contain hidden malicious instructions. 

We are also releasing Argon without cyber guardrails to a select set of trusted defenders, which allows for testing a full breadth of cybersecurity capabilities. Trusted defenders are vetted through our Fairwind Program, a limited access initiative that provides government, critical infrastructure, and cybersecurity partners exclusive, unmitigated access to advanced  models. 

Enterprise customers and partners in our early access program are already seeing strong wins with Argon.

Leaders from Amplitude, Deloitte, and Rakuten share Gemini 4 Argon results

Get started

Starting today, Gemini 4 Argon is available in Gemini for business on the web, desktop, and mobile. Enterprise developers and builders can access Argon via API in Gemini platform under model ID gemini-4-argon, in Google AI Studio, and in Google Antigravity.

Argon launches at an introductory rate of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, 2026, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off. After November 30, standard pricing of $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens will apply. Review the model card and developer guide for complete technical specifications, token limits, and migration instructions.

Cyber defenders can join us at Security Summit to learn how to use Gemini 4 Argon to defend against machine-speed threats and automate remediation.

title: Welcome to Gemini at Work 2026: Introducing the Gemini agent
summary:
Editor’s note: This article is adapted from Thomas Kurian’s keynote address at Gemini at Work 2026. It includes a number of announcements:

  • Gemini, a single, universal agent for work that answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code. 

  • Inline in Workspace, Gemini works directly inside Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Chat, and Calendar, carrying the same memory, skills, and controls it has everywhere else.

  • New data and analytics skills that allow both technical teams and everyday business users to use plain-language questions to get to actionable operational insights in minutes. 

  • Industry-specific specialization with tools, skills, connectors and knowledge specific for financial services and legal teams.

  • How we secure and govern agents through identity and policy management, authorization and permission controls, secure sandboxing, network gateways, and more.

  • Leading cost controls through multi-model orchestration, Smart Routing, real-time spend caps, and more.

  • Customer use cases that showcase the breadth and depth of our customers around the world.

Bringing the best technology to all of you is what drives us at Google Cloud. In the last year, nearly 500 Google Cloud customers each processed more than one trillion tokens. Today, nearly 80% of all Google Cloud customers are using our AI products, and nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise. At that kind of scale, organizations have moved past experimentation and are running their business on it.

Work now starts in the prompt window. 

To meet this moment, today we are excited to announce the Gemini agent: your new single, universal agent for work. It has all of your business context and can be used for everything from knowledge work to answering questions, and from content creation to coding, all from a single prompt box. It plans the work, uses skills and tools, connects to your systems, and brings back something finished — inside the documents, the inbox, and the developer environments you already work in. It chooses the best model for the job, has built-in cost controls, and most importantly, has the security, administration, and governance required by your company.

Introducing the Gemini agent 

Gemini answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code — all in a single agent and a single API. You give it objectives, not instructions. You delegate an outcome and come back to finished work. For an agent to do that, it has to be connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls. Gemini can function as your personal assistant or as a team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department.

The agentic capabilities in Gemini are built around core architectural principles:

  • Unified agent: Gemini is an agent that can answer your questions when you chat with it, work autonomously to complete objectives you assign it, and generate code — all from a single interface. You can assign it work, schedule tasks that need to be completed, or have it respond to events.

  • Omnipresent access: Gemini can be accessed from any device including web, iOS and Android mobile devices, Windows and Mac desktops, and any channel (command line, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or Slack). It can also be integrated into third-party applications and surfaces and operates as a headless agent, meaning it does not need a dedicated user interface.

  • Persistent execution: It runs in the cloud, meaning it maintains a single set of memories, context, and one personalization graph no matter what device or channel you access it on. You never have to re-brief it or wonder which machine you told it to do something on. Work that takes hours or days keeps running after you close your laptop, and it is still there when you come back. 

  • Multi-agent orchestration: Gemini doesn’t work alone. It can dynamically create a roster of sub-agents — temporary, job-specific agents, each with their own identity — to tackle multi-step tasks. Gemini can communicate with these sub-agents to coordinate workflows, including parallel and sequential steps that can run for hours or days. In addition, Gemini can act as a coworker agent — which is more like a team member, with a persistent, defined role and operational presence across days, sessions, and multiple changing responsibilities — and delegate and coordinate tasks. Coworker agents have dedicated identities including their own @agents.company.com emails, their own persistent storage, and only have access to the context that you or your team members provide.

  • Deeply contextual: Gemini arrives already knowing your tools, data, and work history. Whether you ask it a question, assign it an objective, or have it generate code, Gemini learns from every interaction with you. The longer you collaborate with it, the better it understands you and how you work. Teams can create dedicated projects to further optimize the context, skills, and tools Gemini uses when it works with you.  

  • Model choice flexibility: Gemini is the agent, and the model underneath it is a separate choice. It runs each job on the model that fits best — orchestrating across our Gemini family of models and Claude  models from Anthropic today, and other leading private and open models in the future — to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs. The best model for the task is not always the largest one. Matching the model to the work raises accuracy on the difficult jobs and lowers cost on the simple ones. And the leading model changes every few months, so keeping that choice open means your context, your skills, and your data stay put when it does.

Top customers across industries were early testers and are already realizing its benefits: Premium sportswear brand On tested this new dynamic selection capability to accelerate its speed-to-market. This builds on the proven, large-scale multi-model strategies already used by leaders: Shopify blends frontier models for millions of merchants to unlock data and drive sales, and PayPal routes 10 million multi-model requests every week.

Powering Gemini: Skills, tools, and context

Gemini understands your business — everything from pricing to product portfolios to departmental norms — and all the institutional knowledge that makes your company unique. Three capabilities make that possible: tools that connect it to your systems, skills that teach it how your work gets done, and context that lets it remember. 

  • Tools and tools registry: Gemini can securely connect to the software your company already runs, including collaboration tools like Confluence, Microsoft Office, Teams, Slack, and Workspace; development tools like Git and Jira; enterprise platforms like Salesforce and ServiceNow; databases like BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres, and Snowflake; and files on your own desktop. It can also connect and work securely with any Model Context Protocol (MCP) server inside or outside your company network. It also offers an enterprise tools registry, so teams can build and publish tools for the rest of the company. 

  • Skills and skills registry: Skills are reusable sets of instructions, knowledge, or workflows stored as modular prompts that teach agents how to perform specific, multi-step tasks. Gemini ships with a robust global library of skills. Teams or departments can build and publish custom skills to a shared company registry, and you can build your own personal skills. Gemini chooses the right skills and tools to perform a task and continuously learns from each execution, improving its consistency, while saving token costs.

  • Context and memory: Gemini learns from each question you ask it, each objective you assign it, the people you work with, and uses your personal context and your organization's context to personalize and improve the quality of its responses. It keeps four kinds of memory: session memory for the task in front of it, even when it runs for days; semantic memory, a structured knowledge base it builds as it reads documents, talks to people, and works with other agents; procedural memory for how a job gets done, including skills it writes for itself; and episodic memory of everything it has done before. Gemini onboards itself the way a new hire would, learning you, your tools, and your team before it starts.

Customers seeing significant benefits from Gemini Enterprise include:

  • BNP Paribas, a European leader in banking and financial services, is transforming Corporate & Institutional Banking by deploying Gemini Enterprise into LLM@CIB, its internal generative AI assistant available to more than 65,000 employees, to streamline workflows like preparing credit memos and boosting the productivity of customer advisers while maintaining strict enterprise-grade security and data governance.

  • Bradesco, one of Brazil’s largest banking and financial services conglomerates, is streamlining heavy operational workflows by deploying Gemini Enterprise for automated fiscal, accounting, and contractual analysis. The finance team has accelerated proposal reviews, service classification, and budgetary workflows, cutting document review time from 1 hour to 5 minutes while reducing risk inconsistencies by 60% and achieving over 10% in financial efficiencies.

  • Merck is exploring new frontiers in molecular research with the potential to significantly compress discovery timelines while maintaining complete data privacy and security.

  • Orange Spain, a leading telecommunications operator in Spain, is speeding up its digital transformation by deploying more than 1,000 custom Gemini Enterprise agents. Employees across HR, IT, sales, and customer service have built custom agents to automate incident triage, analyze network issues, and retrieve corporate knowledge, boosting operational agility and response times while helping non-technical staff automate daily workflows with zero IT bottlenecks.

  • Santee Cooper, South Carolina’s state-owned electric and water utility, is modernizing its financial planning and grid reliability by deploying a specialized AI model built on Gemini Enterprise. Financial planning teams and utility operators are automating complex financial scenario modeling and query execution using simple natural language and expect to boost modeling speed by up to 75% while mitigating market risk across a $10 billion grid expansion budget.

  • SOMPO, a leading Japanese insurance provider, built over 10,000 custom AI agents across its 34,000 employees to automate tasks like document search and summarization for employee efficiency. Their engineering team used Gemini Enterprise to cut the development time for new models from one week to a single day, freeing up engineers for more important work.

  • Ulta Beauty is helping guests shop 30,000 products by deploying the Ulta AI shopping assistant built with Gemini Enterprise. Online shoppers have translated conversational questions into personalized beauty recommendations, boosting digital sales conversion rates three-fold while skipping traditional search filters to buy the products they love instantly.

  • Wesfarmers, the parent company of Australian retail giants Bunnings, Kmart, and Officeworks, is deploying agents across its portfolio. An internal agent at Bunnings saved staff half a million hours of administrative work, while shopping agents — that help customers discover products and build their carts — have increased conversion rates up to three times higher for Kmart and Officeworks.

Gemini in Google Workspace

Gemini not only answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, and writes your code — it works directly inside Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Chat, and Calendar, carrying the same memory, skills, and controls it has everywhere else. It works inline: in the email thread, in the document, and in the chat space. 

Inside Workspace, Gemini works three ways:

  • Personal assistance: Gemini works as your personal agent and arrives already knowing your calendar, your team, your projects, and how your documents relate to one another. It is briefed before you start.  For example, you can ask Gemini to set up a meeting with the usual team of regional event leads next week, without supplying a single name or email address. Gemini determines who those people are from the membership of your chat space and the thread from your last event, checks their calendars, and starts an email thread to coordinate a time that works, even with external participants. It handles work that spans applications the same way: researching market trends, building a financial model in Sheets, then creating a deck that presents both, without you re-explaining the project at each step.

  • Proactive delegation: Gemini uses this same intelligence to proactively suggest tasks you can delegate to it. For example, if your manager emails you asking for the latest project update as a slide deck, Workspace Intelligence recognizes that as a delegatable task and gives you a single-click option to pass it to Gemini. It applies the same reasoning to your inbox, surfacing the message that matters most rather than the one that arrived last, and explaining why. 

  • A member of your team: You can also use Gemini to create a coworker agent that works with your entire team. You simply describe the role you need, and Gemini creates it. The agent receives its own Workspace account, including an email address, calendar, Drive, and presence in your company directory. Your colleagues work with it the way they work with anyone else, by adding it to a Chat space or @mentioning it. For example, a marketing manager can ask an events coordinator agent in a chat group to draft a launch readiness document, which it posts back to the group when complete. The marketing manager could also tag the agent in a document comment, where it can suggest an edit in the Doc and reply in the comment thread, appearing under its own name in version history. A coworker agent acts under its own identity rather than yours, and it sees only what you share with it. Access follows the sharing and membership your team already uses, and no outside connector holds your data.

Data analysis, data engineering and machine learning 

We are also giving Gemini skills built for specific domains, starting with data.

Data and analytics represent a foundational domain where Gemini transforms business workflows, enabling organizations to move from plain-language questions to actionable operational insights in minutes. We are introducing purpose-built capabilities tailored to both technical teams and everyday business users:

  • For Data and ML engineers: We are extending Gemini with machine learning skills and tools that back every data scientist and data engineer with a team of agents. Engineers describe the outcome they want in plain language, and Gemini generates PySpark code, provides notebooks to edit and test it, trains models, and troubleshoots and fixes pipeline issues on its own.

  • For business users: Anyone in your organization can generate reliable, real-time operational reports simply by asking. Gemini uses operational reporting skills integrated with BigQuery and the Knowledge Catalog to construct and save the query. Once saved, teams can run reports on demand without incurring token costs, guaranteeing consistent, verified answers every time.

Three Google Cloud capabilities keep those answers grounded:

  • Knowledge Catalog: Gemini integrates directly with your Knowledge Catalog to map business definitions once so all agents use them. This deep understanding of your organization’s schemas and business rules for terms like “net margin” and “addressable market” dramatically improves accuracy. Whether your metrics live in Databricks, dbt, LookML, or SAP, Gemini reads them directly where they sit to ensure factual responses.

  • Smart Storage: Ninety percent of enterprise data is unstructured — PDFs, images, scans, and audio recordings — which often remain "dark" and unreadable. Smart Storage changes this by enriching unstructured objects in place and writing context back directly onto the object itself. The intelligence stays where the bytes reside and inherits your existing security posture.

  • Borderless Lakehouse: Organizations should not be forced to move or duplicate their data to use AI. Our borderless Lakehouse allows Gemini to query Amazon S3 and Azure Data Lake with no variable egress fees, read directly from Salesforce Data 360, SAP, and Workday without copying data, and federate open Apache Iceberg tables across Databricks Unity, Snowflake Horizon, and AWS Glue.

You can start by registering data sets that you discover in your lakehouse with the Knowledge Catalog, and then assign Gemini simple or complex analysis to perform. It identifies the necessary data sets from the Knowledge Catalog, generates the necessary SQL, Spark or Python code to calculate the results, and runs the code on our Managed Spark Service with Lightning Engine or in BigQuery. It can also generate charts and build dashboards in the tools your analysts already use.

By grounding its data agents in the Knowledge Catalog, Bloomberg Media lifted its SQL query accuracy by 63% during initial development. As William Anderson, Bloomberg Media’s CTO, noted: “...by grounding our AI in a trusted institutional context, we ensure confidence in the accuracy and quality of every insight generated.”

Additional customers are seeing tremendous value from our data solutions:

  • Deutsche Telekom used BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Knowledge Catalog to build a unified data lakehouse to overcome a fragmented and slow data infrastructure spread across 40+ legacy on-premise systems, allowing their teams to now move ten times faster while addressing European data sovereignty and security requirements.

  • Etsy migrated three petabytes of data to a unified lakehouse. By using BigQuery and open-source Apache Iceberg, they can now perform critical data joins up to 60% faster, allowing them to train models on much larger datasets and better connect buyers with the perfect items.

  • Snap connected its Prism agent directly to its storage archives, cutting technical diagnostic troubleshooting times down from 30 minutes to just 30 seconds.

Industry-specific specializations

Every industry runs on knowledge a general model does not have. We are specializing Gemini for individual industries, with the skills, tools, and knowledge specific to each one. It is now in preview for Financial Services and Legal, and coming soon to Government, Healthcare, and Retail. 

  • Financial Services: Gemini for Financial Services automates what is usually pieced together across many workstreams: investment research, credit analysis, and risk modeling. It draws on trusted financial data from FactSet, LSEG, S&P Global, SEC filings, and your own proprietary repositories. Built with more than 50 foundational skills and designed to satisfy rigorous compliance, it shows its reasoning through confidence scores, explicit methodologies, full data lineage for easy auditing, and source citations you can check. Gemini for Financial Services is already being used by global financial institutions like CME Group and Deutsche Bank.

  • Legal: Gemini inherits matter-level permissions and ethical walls directly from document management platforms like NetDocuments and iManage. Partners like Harvey automate complex legal work while meeting the firm's confidentiality standards, while Onit streamlines contract lifecycle management without exposing privilege. Cooley is building a confidential information redaction agent on Gemini Enterprise for Legal that automates redactions, including personally identifiable information and confidential material, before legal filings go public. In high-stakes litigation, this can cut days of document review while maintaining the firm's rigorous standards for client confidentiality.

In addition, we’ve seen our ecosystem and customers create new vertical applications as well. For example, Deloitte has created a multi-agentic solution to help organizations identify the highest-value opportunities for AI applications for their business. Their Agentic AI blueprint develops operational heat maps to pinpoint areas ready for agentic redesign, accelerating the deployment of custom agentic workflows and achieving up to a 3x faster path to measurable business impact.

Securing and governing agents

Two factors determine whether an enterprise agent program succeeds or stalls: whether you can govern it, and whether you can afford it.

When deploying autonomous agents across an organization, governance comes down to answering four fundamental questions:

  • Who is the agent, and what identity does it have? 

  • What is it allowed to do or what permissions is it granted? 

  • What did it do and where can I see what it did? 

  • What should it never touch?

Identity, policy, and observability answer the first three. The fourth is Agent Gateway.  

  • Identity: Every agent gets its own identity, cryptographically attested and governed like an employee, with least-privilege permissions. That identity is stamped into the logs that capture its work, and into any virtual machine spun up to run code on its behalf.

  • Authorization and permissions: You give each agent fine-grained, role-based access permissions, approved by your organization’s security administrators. When the Gemini agent connects to an external system, its identity is mapped and propagated through industry standards such as OAuth.

  • Auditing: In addition, every action Gemini takes is written to an audit trail and attributed to the agent rather than to a person. Since the identity travels into any virtual machine the agent spins up to run code, you can monitor those logs with our observability tools in real time and catch anomalous behavior before it matters. 

  • Policy management and control: Gemini gives you identity, discovery, governance, and security by default. All Gemini agents execute tasks safely inside an Agent Sandbox with its own network boundary. All traffic — in, out, and between agents — passes through Agent Gateway, an AI network firewall enforcing your organization’s policies in real time. You write the policy once, such as: “agents may not open documents classified Need to Know.” Gemini applies it to every agent in your company instead of checking one agent at a time.

Leading cost controls and spending options

While per-token prices have dropped 98% since 2024, enterprise AI volume has exploded. Running every simple loop through a premium model quickly breaks corporate budgets. We announced new flexible spending options recently and are adding to those today: 

  • Multi-model orchestration: As mentioned earlier, Gemini allows you to choose the right model for the job, and even combine different models for specific tasks in larger projects to deliver optimal quality and lower your cost.

  • Smart routing: Our routing tool automatically triages enterprise workloads so each one runs on the model that delivers maximum performance at the lowest possible cost.

  • Real-time spend caps: You can set a hard limit on a project's AI spend in the Cloud Billing Console, and Gemini enforces it. Gemini monitors token usage and sandbox costs, and if a spend cap is triggered, that project's agent pauses, and you can choose to resume work with a single click in the console. Because the tracking is per project, companies can charge AI costs back to specific departments.

Infrastructure: 80% better price-performance

All of this innovation — the agent, the data, the identity, and everything else — runs on our AI Infrastructure and our models. They are the reason the economics work.

First, our AI infrastructure. We co-design the chips, the network, the data center, and the software that connects it all as one highly-optimized system — our AI Hypercomputer. This vertical integration delivers significantly better price-performance than the generic setups, and we are continuing to push the state of the art here. For example, our latest TPU 8i system delivers 80% better price-performance than the prior generation, making complex, high-value agent tasks both fast and highly affordable.

On top of this silicon sit our models: Argon for frontier reasoning, Flash for speed and volume, Omni for generative media, and Gemma for lightweight, open-weights edge workloads.

The edge capabilities are already real. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory is running Gemma directly on a satellite in orbit, a first for a vision-language model. JPL’s NAVI software analyzes Earth imagery on board the satellite and sends a summary with key information to ground operators.

Supercharged by our ecosystem

We remain committed to choice at every layer of the stack, ensuring you have the freedom to choose the best tech stack for your unique needs.

Inside Gemini, you have a broad choice of third-party agents from leading SaaS providers as well as connectors that are ready to use. They are even easier to discover as collections in the new AI Solution Finder.

Around Gemini, our services ecosystem continues to rapidly scale to meet enterprise demand. Together, in the last month alone, our global consulting partners have put more than a hundred thousand of their developers and consultants through Gemini hackathons.

In addition, Accenture has made a significant investment by establishing a dedicated Gemini Enterprise Business Group to accelerate customer adoption and innovation. Several other partners have also expanded their commitments to support the growing demand for Gemini, including establishing specialized centers of excellence and training Gemini credentialed practitioners to help customers build and deploy production-grade agents faster.

title: Innovation in Ireland: How Irish brands scale with Gemini Enterprise

title: What’s new in AI infrastructure and orchestration in September
summary:
We hereby declare September to be scalability month! As the world prepares for a surge of agentic fleets, we are shoring up our AI infrastructure and orchestration offerings to gracefully — and quickly — respond to that demand, all while maintaining workload isolation and security, and keeping costs in check. Read on to learn how these enhancements manifest across Google Cloud’s compute, network, storage, and orchestration offerings, plus new ways customers are using Google Cloud AI infrastructure, and third-party industry validation of our strategy.

Product, technology, and tools updates

Google Kubernetes Engine updates: The GKE team is all about improving the scalability of the platform, and in September, those improvements came in many shapes and sizes:

  • New feature: Need an execution runtime with higher density for your agentic workloads? We engineered the new open-source GKE Agent Substrate to run millions of sandboxes with 10x higher density than standard container runtimes. Agent Substrate also delivers sub-500ms resume operations at over 500 suspend/resume activations per second with a native zero-trust kernel and network isolation. 

  • Product update: GKE now has scale-to-zero capabilities built-in. No need to configure complex components to scale your workloads down, thanks to the HPA with the Autoscaling Metric and support for KEP-2021, which do the job for you, out of the box. Read the blog to learn more. 

  • Product update: Further, the GKE HPA (with the above-mentioned Autoscaling Metric) now lets you scale up and down based on custom PromQL metrics, in addition to standard metrics, allowing you to trigger workloads according to conditions that are meaningful and unique to your business. Read more here. 

  • New feature: Yet another scalability feature is GKE Pod snapshots, which lets you save the running state of your workload, including CPU and GPU memory, and restore it on demand. According to internal tests, GKE Pod snapshots can reduce AI inference start-up by as much as 89%. Learn more here.

  • New migration tool: Finally, if you’ve always wanted to migrate your container workloads from AWS EKS to GKE but feared a daunting, high-friction engineering endeavor, we’ve just launched GKE agentic migration, a purpose-built agent plugin that replaces brittle, ad-hoc prompting with an AI-assisted migration pipeline protected by deterministic guardrails. Designed as a compilation of agent skills and a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, it uses AI to translate complex AWS EKS IaC and Kubernetes manifests directly into GKE landing zones. Get started with the onboarding guide.

  • Feature updates: Reinforcement learning (RL) and evaluation workloads are a beast: In a standard agentic RL loop, an LLM policy generates actions like code snippets on GPUs and executes them inside isolated CPU sandboxes to observe a reward signal. However, when scaling up this loop to support tens of thousands of parallel rollouts, infrastructure bottlenecks emerge, for instance idle accelerators, image cardinality, and a saturated control plane. To help, we developed GKE Agent Sandbox optimized for RL, plus an Agent Sandbox RL orchestration SDK and native integrations for popular RL gyms and harnesses. All are now generally available, and you can learn more here.

Storage updates: AI trains and creates lots of data, and that data has to live somewhere — in block storage systems, file systems, object stores and databases. We announced enhancements to our storage portfolio to help this critical layer roll with the agentic punches:  

  • Product update: Filestore agent volumes offer high-performance, elastic, persistent file storage for agentic workloads. Thanks to its tight integration with GKE Agent Substrate and GKE Agent Sandbox, Filestore agent volumes automatically allocates and attaches a dedicated, isolated file workspace to GKE agent sandboxes in milliseconds. Request access to the preview here.

title: Empower your agents with the Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server
summary:
Today, we’re expanding our ecosystem of managed remote MCP servers by introducing the Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server in preview.

Powered by the popular gcloud and bq (BigQuery) command-line tools, this new server gives AI agents immediate, broad access to command-line operations for managing Google Cloud infrastructure and working with advanced BigQuery workflows securely and seamlessly. 

Why CLI matters for AI agents

Agents are increasingly performing complex cloud operations, but standardizing how they interact with backend systems remains a challenge. The Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server bridges this gap by packaging the versatility of hundreds of gcloud and bq commands into one single MCP server. This results in two strong benefits for the agent:

  • Higher-level abstractions: CLI commands package complex multi-step workflows, validation checks, and high-level operations into unified commands rather than requiring multi-step API orchestration.

  • Leverages model training: LLMs are heavily pre-trained on public command-line documentation, syntaxes, and usage examples, making CLI invocation intuitive and highly accurate for models.

The benefits of putting CLI behind remote MCP

Managing cloud infrastructure with AI agents traditionally requires installing and maintaining Google Cloud CLI binaries inside agent execution environments. The Cloud CLI remote MCP server bridges CLI capabilities with MCP benefits by providing an isolated execution sandbox on Google Cloud infrastructure. This solves key infrastructure challenges:

  • Simplified dependency and runtime management: For teams building custom agents, maintaining local CLI versions and dependencies across dev, test, and production environments creates operational overhead. Remote MCP eliminates local installations and runtime maintenance.

  • Access for web-based agent endpoints: Web-hosted agent platforms and web interfaces (such as Gemini Enterprise and other hosted enterprise agent platforms) run in environments where users cannot control or install local packages. Remote MCP enables secure, managed access to Google Cloud CLI operations directly from these surfaces.

Enterprise-grade security and governance

Connecting an AI agent to your infrastructure requires strict, enterprise-ready safeguards. This remote server leverages Google Cloud's standard identity and governance frameworks to keep your environments secure:

  • Zero ambient credentials: The server isolates execution in a network-restricted proxy boundary with no ambient credentials. Authentication and authorization are handled through Agent Identity, OAuth 2.0, and Identity and Access Management (IAM).

  • Strict policy enforcement: Every command executed through the remote MCP server is run with the permissions of the authenticated caller identity. Both standard IAM permissions and organization policy service constraints are strictly enforced against downstream target resources.

  • Advanced protection with Model Armor: To minimize the risks associated with AI tool calling, the Cloud CLI remote MCP server integrates with Model Armor. You can proactively screen LLM prompts and responses to protect against risks like prompt injection and malicious inputs.

  • Cloud audit logging: The Cloud CLI remote MCP server can be configured to log every tool invocation to Audit Logs (Data Access logs under cloudcli.googleapis.com/mcp). Security teams can gain full visibility into caller identities, OAuth clients, and IAM authorization decisions (mcp.googleapis.com/tools.call) without exposing sensitive command payloads or personally identifiable information (PII).

Connecting to the Google Cloud CLI Remote MCP Server

Integrating cloud management into your agents no longer requires packaging Google Cloud CLI binaries, managing local execution runtimes, or maintaining dependencies inside agent container images. Because the Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server implements the standard Model Context Protocol, any MCP-compatible agent platform or orchestration runtime can connect immediately via standard configuration:

code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '{\r\n "mcpServers": {\r\n "google-cloud-cli": {\r\n "uri": "https://cloudcli.googleapis.com/mcp",\r\n ...\r\n }\r\n }\r\n}'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f30c4123910>)])]>

Your agent immediately gains access to execute gcloud and bq commands in a secure, network-isolated cloud sandbox.

Authentication is handled via keyless Agent Identity for hosted Google Cloud platforms, or standard OAuth 2.0 for external runtimes. For authentication options, see the MCP Authentication Guide.

Bringing infrastructure management to agents

The Cloud CLI remote MCP server exposes two powerful tools, run_gcloud_command and run_bq_command, giving your AI agents broad, immediate access to Google Cloud operations through natural language.

Managing cloud infrastructure with run_gcloud_command

With run_gcloud_command, agents can execute the full breadth of gcloud operations to manage, diagnose, and secure your Google Cloud environment. An example follows:

  • Observability and incident diagnostics: An agent streamlines incident diagnostics by automating command execution and reducing context-switching across tools.

Extending BigQuery operations with the run_bq_command tool

While the BigQuery MCP server already helps organizations analyze and explore data using AI agents, with the introduction of run_bq_command, agents can now tackle advanced BigQuery tasks such as resource allocation, job monitoring, and task scheduling by unlocking the full scope of bq CLI functionality. Key capabilities include:

  • Automating scheduled queries: An agent utilizes BigQuery Data Transfer Service configurations to schedule queries automatically. 

  • Job and resource management: Gain deep insight into query execution details, including processed data volume, slot usage, and execution plans, as well as managing reservations.

  • Access and permissions control: Data administrators and owners can inspect and update table permissions directly through the agent.

Pricing and availability

The Google Cloud CLI MCP server is available today in public preview. There is no additional charge to use the MCP server itself. You pay only for the GCP resources you create and any applicable data transfer costs.

To get started, enable the Cloud CLI Execution API (`cloudcli.googleapis.com`) in your Google Cloud project, grant the required MCP Tool User (`roles/mcp.toolUser`) IAM role to your agent or user identity, and configure your MCP client to connect to `cloudcli.googleapis.com/mcp`.
